work.title: The Third Part of King Henry the Sixth
work.author: William Shakespeare

content.text: Enter Richard (Duke of Gloucester), George (Duke of Clarence), Somerset and Montague.

lines.text: Now tell me, brother Clarence, what think you
lines.plainText: Now tell me brother Clarence what think you

lines.text: Of this new marriage with the Lady Grey?
lines.plainText: Of this new marriage with the Lady Grey

lines.text: Hath not our brother made a worthy choice?
lines.plainText: Hath not our brother made a worthy choice

lines.text: Alas, you know 'tis far from hence to France!
lines.plainText: Alas you know 'tis far from hence to France

lines.text: How could he stay till Warwick made return?
lines.plainText: How could he stay till Warwick made return

lines.text: My lords, forbear this talk; here comes the King.
lines.plainText: My lords forbear this talk here comes the King

content.text: Flourish. Enter King Edward, attended; Lady Grey as Queen Elizabeth; Pembroke, Stafford, Hastings and others. Four stand on one side, and four on the other.

lines.text: And his well-chosen bride.
lines.plainText: And his wellchosen bride

lines.text: I mind to tell him plainly what I think.
lines.plainText: I mind to tell him plainly what I think

lines.text: Now, brother of Clarence, how like you our choice,
lines.plainText: Now brother of Clarence how like you our choice

lines.text: That you stand pensive as half malcontent?
lines.plainText: That you stand pensive as half malcontent

lines.text: As well as Lewis of France or the Earl of Warwick,
lines.plainText: As well as Lewis of France or the Earl of Warwick

lines.text: Which are so weak of courage and in judgment
lines.plainText: Which are so weak of courage and in judgment

lines.text: That they'll take no offence at our abuse.
lines.plainText: That they'll take no offence at our abuse

lines.text: Suppose they take offence without a cause,
lines.plainText: Suppose they take offence without a cause

lines.text: They are but Lewis and Warwick; I am Edward,
lines.plainText: They are but Lewis and Warwick I am Edward

lines.text: Your King and Warwick's, and must have my will.
lines.plainText: Your King and Warwick's and must have my will

lines.text: And shall have your will, because our King.
lines.plainText: And shall have your will because our King

lines.text: Yet hasty marriage seldom proveth well.
lines.plainText: Yet hasty marriage seldom proveth well

lines.text: Yea, brother Richard, are you offended too?
lines.plainText: Yea brother Richard are you offended too

lines.text: Not I.
lines.plainText: Not I

lines.text: No, God forbid that I should wish them severed
lines.plainText: No God forbid that I should wish them severed

lines.text: Whom God hath joined together. Ay, and 'twere pity
lines.plainText: Whom God hath joined together Ay and 'twere pity

lines.text: To sunder them that yoke so well together.
lines.plainText: To sunder them that yoke so well together

lines.text: Setting your scorns and your mislike aside,
lines.plainText: Setting your scorns and your mislike aside

lines.text: Tell me some reason why the Lady Grey
lines.plainText: Tell me some reason why the Lady Grey

lines.text: Should not become my wife and England's queen.
lines.plainText: Should not become my wife and England's queen

lines.text: And you too, Somerset and Montague,
lines.plainText: And you too Somerset and Montague

lines.text: Speak freely what you think.
lines.plainText: Speak freely what you think

lines.text: Then this is mine opinion: that King Lewis
lines.plainText: Then this is mine opinion that King Lewis

lines.text: Becomes your enemy for mocking him
lines.plainText: Becomes your enemy for mocking him

lines.text: About the marriage of the Lady Bona.
lines.plainText: About the marriage of the Lady Bona

lines.text: And Warwick, doing what you gave in charge,
lines.plainText: And Warwick doing what you gave in charge

lines.text: Is now dishonoured by this new marriage.
lines.plainText: Is now dishonoured by this new marriage

lines.text: What if both Lewis and Warwick be appeased
lines.plainText: What if both Lewis and Warwick be appeased

lines.text: By such invention as I can devise?
lines.plainText: By such invention as I can devise

lines.text: Yet to have joined with France in such alliance
lines.plainText: Yet to have joined with France in such alliance

lines.text: Would more have strengthened this our commonwealth
lines.plainText: Would more have strengthened this our commonwealth

lines.text: 'Gainst foreign storms than any home-bred marriage.
lines.plainText: 'Gainst foreign storms than any homebred marriage

lines.text: Why, knows not Montague that of itself
lines.plainText: Why knows not Montague that of itself

lines.text: England is safe, if true within itself?
lines.plainText: England is safe if true within itself

lines.text: But the safer when 'tis backed with France.
lines.plainText: But the safer when 'tis backed with France

lines.text: 'Tis better using France than trusting France.
lines.plainText: 'Tis better using France than trusting France

lines.text: Let us be backed with God and with the seas
lines.plainText: Let us be backed with God and with the seas

lines.text: Which He hath giv'n for fence impregnable,
lines.plainText: Which He hath giv'n for fence impregnable

lines.text: And with their helps only defend ourselves.
lines.plainText: And with their helps only defend ourselves

lines.text: In them and in ourselves our safety lies.
lines.plainText: In them and in ourselves our safety lies

lines.text: For this one speech Lord Hastings well deserves
lines.plainText: For this one speech Lord Hastings well deserves

lines.text: To have the heir of the Lord Hungerford.
lines.plainText: To have the heir of the Lord Hungerford

lines.text: Ay, what of that? It was my will and grant;
lines.plainText: Ay what of that It was my will and grant

lines.text: And for this once my will shall stand for law.
lines.plainText: And for this once my will shall stand for law

lines.text: And yet, methinks, your Grace hath not done well
lines.plainText: And yet methinks your Grace hath not done well

lines.text: To give the heir and daughter of Lord Scales
lines.plainText: To give the heir and daughter of Lord Scales

lines.text: Unto the brother of your loving bride.
lines.plainText: Unto the brother of your loving bride

lines.text: She better would have fitted me or Clarence;
lines.plainText: She better would have fitted me or Clarence

lines.text: But in your bride you bury brotherhood.
lines.plainText: But in your bride you bury brotherhood

lines.text: Or else you would not have bestowed the heir
lines.plainText: Or else you would not have bestowed the heir

lines.text: Of the Lord Bonville on your new wife's son,
lines.plainText: Of the Lord Bonville on your new wife's son

lines.text: And leave your brothers to go speed elsewhere.
lines.plainText: And leave your brothers to go speed elsewhere

lines.text: Alas, poor Clarence, is it for a wife
lines.plainText: Alas poor Clarence is it for a wife

lines.text: That thou art malcontent? I will provide thee.
lines.plainText: That thou art malcontent I will provide thee

lines.text: In choosing for yourself you showed your judgment,
lines.plainText: In choosing for yourself you showed your judgment

lines.text: Which being shallow, you shall give me leave
lines.plainText: Which being shallow you shall give me leave

lines.text: To play the broker in mine own behalf;
lines.plainText: To play the broker in mine own behalf

lines.text: And to that end I shortly mind to leave you.
lines.plainText: And to that end I shortly mind to leave you

lines.text: Leave me or tarry, Edward will be king,
lines.plainText: Leave me or tarry Edward will be king

lines.text: And not be tied unto his brother's will.
lines.plainText: And not be tied unto his brother's will

lines.text: My lords, before it pleased his Majesty
lines.plainText: My lords before it pleased his Majesty

lines.text: To raise my state to title of a queen,
lines.plainText: To raise my state to title of a queen

lines.text: Do me but right, and you must all confess
lines.plainText: Do me but right and you must all confess

lines.text: That I was not ignoble of descent,
lines.plainText: That I was not ignoble of descent

lines.text: And meaner than myself have had like fortune.
lines.plainText: And meaner than myself have had like fortune

lines.text: But as this title honours me and mine,
lines.plainText: But as this title honours me and mine

lines.text: So your dislikes, to whom I would be pleasing,
lines.plainText: So your dislikes to whom I would be pleasing

lines.text: Doth cloud my joys with danger and with sorrow.
lines.plainText: Doth cloud my joys with danger and with sorrow

lines.text: My love, forbear to fawn upon their frowns.
lines.plainText: My love forbear to fawn upon their frowns

lines.text: What danger or what sorrow can befall thee
lines.plainText: What danger or what sorrow can befall thee

lines.text: So long as Edward is thy constant friend
lines.plainText: So long as Edward is thy constant friend

lines.text: And their true sovereign, whom they must obey?
lines.plainText: And their true sovereign whom they must obey

lines.text: Nay, whom they shall obey, and love thee too,
lines.plainText: Nay whom they shall obey and love thee too

lines.text: Unless they seek for hatred at my hands;
lines.plainText: Unless they seek for hatred at my hands

lines.text: Which if they do, yet will I keep thee safe,
lines.plainText: Which if they do yet will I keep thee safe

lines.text: And they shall feel the vengeance of my wrath.
lines.plainText: And they shall feel the vengeance of my wrath

lines.text: [Aside.] I hear, yet say not much, but think the more.
lines.plainText: Aside I hear yet say not much but think the more

lines.text: Now, messenger, what letters or what news
lines.plainText: Now messenger what letters or what news

lines.text: From France?
lines.plainText: From France

lines.text: My sovereign liege, no letters, and few words,
lines.plainText: My sovereign liege no letters and few words

lines.text: But such as I, without your special pardon,
lines.plainText: But such as I without your special pardon

lines.text: Dare not relate.
lines.plainText: Dare not relate

lines.text: Go to, we pardon thee. Therefore, in brief,
lines.plainText: Go to we pardon thee Therefore in brief

lines.text: Tell me their words as near as thou canst guess them.
lines.plainText: Tell me their words as near as thou canst guess them

lines.text: What answer makes King Lewis unto our letters?
lines.plainText: What answer makes King Lewis unto our letters

lines.text: At my depart these were his very words:
lines.plainText: At my depart these were his very words

lines.text: "Go tell false Edward, thy supposed king,
lines.plainText: Go tell false Edward thy supposed king

lines.text: That Lewis of France is sending over maskers
lines.plainText: That Lewis of France is sending over maskers

lines.text: To revel it with him and his new bride."
lines.plainText: To revel it with him and his new bride

lines.text: Is Lewis so brave? Belike he thinks me Henry.
lines.plainText: Is Lewis so brave Belike he thinks me Henry

lines.text: But what said Lady Bona to my marriage?
lines.plainText: But what said Lady Bona to my marriage

lines.text: These were her words, uttered with mild disdain:
lines.plainText: These were her words uttered with mild disdain

lines.text: "Tell him, in hope he'll prove a widower shortly,
lines.plainText: Tell him in hope he'll prove a widower shortly

lines.text: I'll wear the willow garland for his sake."
lines.plainText: I'll wear the willow garland for his sake

lines.text: I blame not her; she could say little less;
lines.plainText: I blame not her she could say little less

lines.text: She had the wrong. But what said Henry's queen?
lines.plainText: She had the wrong But what said Henry's queen

lines.text: For I have heard that she was there in place.
lines.plainText: For I have heard that she was there in place

lines.text: "Tell him," quoth she "my mourning weeds are done,
lines.plainText: Tell him quoth she my mourning weeds are done

lines.text: And I am ready to put armour on."
lines.plainText: And I am ready to put armour on

lines.text: Belike she minds to play the Amazon.
lines.plainText: Belike she minds to play the Amazon

lines.text: But what said Warwick to these injuries?
lines.plainText: But what said Warwick to these injuries

lines.text: He, more incensed against your Majesty
lines.plainText: He more incensed against your Majesty

lines.text: Than all the rest, discharged me with these words:
lines.plainText: Than all the rest discharged me with these words

lines.text: "Tell him from me that he hath done me wrong,
lines.plainText: Tell him from me that he hath done me wrong

lines.text: And therefore I'll uncrown him ere 't be long."
lines.plainText: And therefore I'll uncrown him ere 't be long

lines.text: Ha! Durst the traitor breathe out so proud words?
lines.plainText: Ha Durst the traitor breathe out so proud words

lines.text: Well, I will arm me, being thus forewarned.
lines.plainText: Well I will arm me being thus forewarned

lines.text: They shall have wars and pay for their presumption.
lines.plainText: They shall have wars and pay for their presumption

lines.text: But say, is Warwick friends with Margaret?
lines.plainText: But say is Warwick friends with Margaret

lines.text: Ay, gracious sovereign, they are so linked in friendship
lines.plainText: Ay gracious sovereign they are so linked in friendship

lines.text: That young Prince Edward marries Warwick's daughter.
lines.plainText: That young Prince Edward marries Warwick's daughter

lines.text: Belike the elder; Clarence will have the younger.
lines.plainText: Belike the elder Clarence will have the younger

lines.text: Now, brother king, farewell, and sit you fast,
lines.plainText: Now brother king farewell and sit you fast

lines.text: For I will hence to Warwick's other daughter;
lines.plainText: For I will hence to Warwick's other daughter

lines.text: That, though I want a kingdom, yet in marriage
lines.plainText: That though I want a kingdom yet in marriage

lines.text: I may not prove inferior to yourself.
lines.plainText: I may not prove inferior to yourself

lines.text: You that love me and Warwick, follow me.
lines.plainText: You that love me and Warwick follow me

lines.text: [Aside.] Not I. My thoughts aim at a further matter;
lines.plainText: Aside Not I My thoughts aim at a further matter

lines.text: I stay not for the love of Edward, but the crown.
lines.plainText: I stay not for the love of Edward but the crown

lines.text: Clarence and Somerset both gone to Warwick!
lines.plainText: Clarence and Somerset both gone to Warwick

lines.text: Yet am I armed against the worst can happen,
lines.plainText: Yet am I armed against the worst can happen

lines.text: And haste is needful in this desperate case.
lines.plainText: And haste is needful in this desperate case

lines.text: Pembroke and Stafford, you in our behalf
lines.plainText: Pembroke and Stafford you in our behalf

lines.text: Go levy men and make prepare for war;
lines.plainText: Go levy men and make prepare for war

lines.text: They are already, or quickly will be, landed.
lines.plainText: They are already or quickly will be landed

lines.text: Myself in person will straight follow you.
lines.plainText: Myself in person will straight follow you

lines.text: So God help Montague as he proves true!
lines.plainText: So God help Montague as he proves true

lines.text: And Hastings as he favours Edward's cause!
lines.plainText: And Hastings as he favours Edward's cause

lines.text: Now, brother Richard, will you stand by us?
lines.plainText: Now brother Richard will you stand by us

lines.text: Ay, in despite of all that shall withstand you.
lines.plainText: Ay in despite of all that shall withstand you

lines.text: Why, so! Then am I sure of victory.
lines.plainText: Why so Then am I sure of victory

lines.text: Now, therefore, let us hence, and lose no hour
lines.plainText: Now therefore let us hence and lose no hour

lines.text: Till we meet Warwick with his foreign power.
lines.plainText: Till we meet Warwick with his foreign power
